**Result:** IFIT1 canonical CDS = **1437 bp** (478 aa); MS4A1 CDS = **894 bp** (297 aa). Ratio = 1437/894 ≈ **1.61×** — well short of 2× (which would require ≥1788 bp). Even the shortest IFIT1 isoform (1344 bp) gives 1.50×. Answer: **no**.

<solution>
IFIT1 is not at least twice as long as MS4A1.

- IFIT1 (NM_001548.5, isoform 1): CDS = 1437 bp (478 aa). Alternative isoform 3 transcripts (NM_001270927–30) = 1344 bp (447 aa).
- MS4A1 (NM_021950.4 / NM_152866.3 / NM_152867.2): CDS = 894 bp (297 aa) in all three RefSeq transcripts.

Ratio: 1437 / 894 ≈ 1.61× (and 1344 / 894 ≈ 1.50× for the short isoform) — both below the 2× threshold (1788 bp).
